newsitem.title: USA: Second accuser says top U.S. soldier sought sex.
newsitem.headline: Second accuser says top U.S. soldier sought sex.

text.p: A woman sergeant testified Friday that the Army's top enlisted man relentlessly pursued her for sex, then asked her to hide that from investigators probing the high-profile sex scandal.

In what appeared a serious blow to the defence of Gene McKinney, who holds the title of Sergeant Major of the Army, prosecutors played a tape recording of a phone conversation in which McKinney is heard asking the woman to limit what she told Army investigators.

McKinney, 46, considered a charismatic and popular chief advocate for the Army's enlisted soldiers, faces 18 charges of sexual misconduct including indecent assault, adultery and obstruction of justice involving four service women.
It is one of a series of cases that has rattled the Army as it attempts to cope with sexual relations within America's fighting force, which includes an increasing number of women.

Friday's testimony came from a staff sergeant who was the second woman to accuse McKinney in a preliminary hearing to determine if McKinney will be court-martialed. The session was called off early because she had laryngitis.
"You don't have to get involved," McKinney was heard telling her on the tape, referring to the investigation against him.

Later he added, "All you have to do is tell them we talked a lot. You called the office and we talked about career development stuff. That's all they need to know. Period. ... Just tell them no inappropriateness at all, just that we talked."

But earlier the woman testified that McKinney, from inside his private Pentagon office, hugged and kissed her against her wishes, rubbing his erect penis against her torso, and that he offered her a job as a travel assistant so that "we could go to discreet hotels."

Under questioning from government prosecutors, the woman said she met McKinney at a 1995 Army convention, when he continually invited her to his hotel room, at one point saying how he could easily bring her to climax with one finger.
She also testified that McKinney sought relations with her while his wife was in Florida tending to their son, who was in a coma following a road accident.
McKinney's wife, Wilhemina, has supported her husband all along and listened intently to the testimony from the gallery.

The Army officer overseeing the hearing asked the media not to publish the woman's name because she is in a witness protection programme. She testified to receiving threats since she began cooperating with investigators.

One day the words "die bitch" were carved into her apartment door and later someone entered her apartment, ripped the head off a stuffed animal and stole documents from her kitchen table, including a copy of a statement against McKinney that she gave to investigators, she said.

The case against McKinney began when one alleged victim grew incensed that he had been named to a high-level panel on sexual harassment in the wake of another scandal in which male drill instructors were having sex with women trainees.
McKinney has vigorously denied all the charges against him, and one of his lawyers said one alleged victim completely fabricated her story.
If the case goes to court-martial and if McKinney is convicted on all counts, he faces up to 45 years in prison.

Friday's witness and one who preceded her have portrayed McKinney as a man who made unwanted sexual advances toward soldiers subject to his orders, bragging of his love-making skills and threatening their careers if they failed to give in to his desires.

The first woman to testify said she finally relented and had unwanted sex with McKinney while she was nearly eight months pregnant. Both women said McKinney's position of power weighed heavily on them.
